title: Antisocial Responses to the “Coal to Gas” Regulation: An Unintended Consequence of a Residential Energy Policy
authors: Jing Wen Cao; Tracy Xiao Liu; Rong Ma; Ang Sun
near_miss_reason: The village-month staggered DiD qualifies on design (binary cwhp switches on in October of each village's treatment_year; six adoption cohorts 2014-2019 inside the 2014-2019 panel; 11 villages never treated in-window; village FE plus province-by-year-month FE; cluster village), but every reported village-level regression, including the did_imputation event studies, adds five time-varying village-month weather controls (temp prcp pressure wspeed sund). No column is reported without them.
eligible_reason: Not eligible as reported: all village-level reghdfe and did_imputation specifications include time-varying weather controls. Individual-level regressions (individual.do) are cross-sectional post-treatment comparisons with PSM weights, not panel DiD. County-level PM regressions (pm_county_month.do) use a continuous regressor (fcn, number of pollution trajectories).
design_notes: Data ft_village_month.dta: 110 villages x 72 months (2014m1-2019m12), 7,920 rows; variables villagecd, countycd, year, month, treatment_year, ft5 (fire count within 5 km), area5 (burned area), pm. Treatment (ft_village_month.do lines 50-51): gen cwhp = year>treatment_year; replace cwhp=1 if year==treatment_year & month>=10. treatment_year distribution over villages: 2014:1, 2015:2, 2016:8, 2017:64, 2018:15, 2019:9, 2020:3, 2021:1, missing:7 (the last three groups are never treated within the panel). Outcomes: ftp5 = (ft5>0), lnft5 = ln(ft5+1), lnarea5 = ln(area5+1), pm. FE: absorb(villagecd provcd#year#month); provcd merged from weather file. Cluster villagecd. Weather controls merged from village_weather_year_month.dta (temp prcp pressure wspeed sund). ftseason = months 2,3,4,10,11,12 (straw-burning season). Event study (Figure 4 / Appendix Table A3): did_imputation with unit = village_month (village x calendar month-of-year group), time = year, gvar = meigaiyear_month (first treated year of that village-month cell), fe(village_month provcd#year#month), horizons(0/4), pretrends(4), controls(weather), cluster villagecd. Seasonal re-weighting loops (aweight=month_weight), bootstrap heterogeneity tests (Tables 6-8, 10, fweight=fq), and alternative radii (ftp4/ftp6, Appendix Table A2) all keep the weather controls.
main_or_robustness: main (village-level straw-burning results: Table 3, Figure 4, Tables 4-10, Appendix Tables A2-A4, A7-A9, A11)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: treatment_year 2014-2019 (6 cohorts with treated observations in the panel; the 2014 cohort is a single village untreated only in Jan-Sep 2014). 11 villages untreated throughout (treatment_year 2020, 2021 or missing).

lines 86, 89 (lnft5, lnarea5); lines 92-98 use ftseason==0 as a placebo season

specs.exclusion_reason: time-varying weather controls inside did_imputation controls()

data_access: unclear (all village-month analysis .dta files are shipped and look like real data; README does not describe sources, restrictions or any synthetic status)
replication_feasible: yes for the near-miss specifications (the TWFE and BJS regressions run from the shipped files once the weather controls are dropped)
screener_notes: Article text not available; table numbers taken from do-file comments and README. The design is a clean staggered village-level adoption with never-treated villages and a reported BJS imputation event study, so this is a strong near-miss candidate if the secondary category admits dropping weather controls. Note that the did_imputation unit is village x calendar-month rather than village. Individual-level analyses (dictator and public-goods games) are single post-treatment cross-sections and do not qualify.
